provenance: Synthetic, authored for RecipeBox. No copied recipe text.
notes: Two sources of gluten: the wheat flour, and oats, which are gluten-free as a grain and routinely contaminated in practice. The caveat is not politeness — ADR 0016 forbids implying an allergen requirement is met, and a cook with coeliac disease acting on 'this is now gluten-free' is the harm.

steps.text: Brown 1/2 cup butter in a pan and let it cool.
Rub the remaining 1/2 cup butter into the flour, sugars, salt and oats until it clumps.
Press two thirds of the crumble into the tin, spread the jam, scatter the rest. Bake at 350°F for 35 minutes in a 9x9-inch tin.

answer.summary: I would swap the wheat flour for a gluten-free blend and add a little xanthan gum so the crumble still clumps.
tradeoffs: A gluten-free crumble browns faster and is more fragile when warm. Let the bars cool fully in the tin.
uncertainties: I cannot guarantee this is safe for coeliac disease. Use a certified gluten-free blend, and check the label on your oats — oats are gluten-free as a grain and are very often contaminated in the mill.
